newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds up in quiet trade, outlook uneventful.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds up in quiet trade, outlook uneventful.

text.p: Danish bond prices edged up slightly in a quiet market on Tuesday with dealers seeing little activity ahead with the focus mainly on EMU developments.
"There's nothing much going on and turnover is relatively low. We seem to have entered a calm period waiting for new EMU signals from France," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.04 point from the start at 111.24, yielding 6.28 percent in turnover of below 200 million crowns, while the forthcoming seven percent 2007 benchmark was 0.05 point higher at 103.83, with a 6.47 percent yield and 600 million crown turnover.
The 2006's June future fell 0.04 point to 111.20 with 230 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.10 point to 89.40.
The crown traded at an unchanged 3.8075 per mark at 1120 GMT.
The 2006 benchmark's 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 50 basis points from the start of trading with the seven percent 2007-bund differential one bp narrower at 68.
